"Gather round the fire, as I tell you the take of the great giant, the protector of the ruined city of Lejir." A few people in the tavern headed over, there was little better to do, and the seats were near the freshly-lit fire. "Many aons ago there was a great kingdom, run by the king Assegai, he owned nearly all the world, and his legend is told throughout the land. Many of you have him to thank for even being here, with his rule he brought peace, he brought prosperity. He was the greatest king the world has known, and all who resided in his lands would agree." The storyteller spead his arms wide. "Just think of that, an entire kingdom where every man woman and child loves their king!" There were murmers from the tavern, and a few other patrons shuffled over to hear what the storyteller had to say.

He carried on, "For 46 years this king ruled, he layed down aqueducts, stadiums, statues and monuments. He advanced the culture and livelihood of the people by hundreds of years within the space of his reign. The king lived for 62 years, but his death was not natural." The storyteller paused now, baiting the audience to ask him to continue. "But what happened then?" asked one of the drunkards, giving in to the storyteller's bait. The storyteller threw a log onto the fire, and while a cascade of sparks flew up into the chimney he roared: "A giant came, and destroyed the king's fair city" there was a gasp from the crowd, but before the audience could catch their breath he carried on. "A gigantic beast he was, with stone armour. His foor alone could crush this whole inn in one stomp, his roar could topple towers, his footsteps would shake the foundations of even the largest fort. This giant marched upon the city, reducing it to rubble."

"The king came then, and asked the giant 'Why would you destroy my fair city, why do you relish in the slaughter of my people?' The giant didn't even give him his answer before he crushed Assegai under his mighty fist." He let the shock sink into the audience, most of the tavern had gathered around by this point. "The people of the city that were lucky enough to have their lives fled over the desert and sought shelter in the rest of the kingdom. The city of Lejir is still empty to this day, and the giant roams around, destroying anyone that comes close."

There was a great applause as the story ended, but a voice cut through it like thunder. "It's a cute tale you tell, certain to entertain, but it would be nice if you didn't spread lies about the old king."

The story teller frowned, but decided to issue a challenge instead of refuting him completely: "How would you tell the story then, stranger in black?"

"There was a once a great king, that much is true, and he rules a great kingdom. But he did not stay great. For many years near the end of his rule greed got the better of him, he grew corrupt by the gold that his kingdom was earning him. He knew his popularity dwindled, so he went to the one place he could change that." Now the stranger gestured to the crowd. "Tell me, why would you build a city in the middle of the desert, with no water for many miles, you even said how he gave us aqueducts, it was because of the location of his 'great city'." The audience looked confused now, the stranger made a good point.

Just as the storyteller was about to chime in the stranger cut him off, "The reason is because Lejir is sited at one of the knots of magical power. The great king Assegai hired mages to brainwash his people into following him, even as he rose taxes, those monuments you mentioned? They were of him, they were built with gold stolen from his people, the labour for them was from people that had no choice whether they wanted to follow him or not. doesn't it seem weird to you that everyone supported the king? Not one soul in an entire kingdom disliked him?" The crowd seemed to be changing opinion now, as some hurled questions at the storyteller.

"The giant was summoned by one of the king's own mages, he sought out the giant because he no longer agreed with what he was being tasked to do. The giant came, and yes he destroyed the city, but the king never asked him about the people, the king asked the giant if he could keep his gold, even if the giant killed the city. The giant slayed a corrupt and cruel leader, and since then has guarded the knot of magic so nobody can abuse it's power again." The audience looked accusingly at the storyteller. It wasn't too much of a surprize when he fled the inn.

Over time I've found two little applications that really helped me in dealing with procrastination and time-management. I've tried others, and there are a myriad of options available (please link any that you know of or personally use!) but these two work for me.

The first is RescueTime, as the accurate tracking of how I spend my time while sitting in front of my laptop is really, really useful. The second is StayFocusd, which despite missing an 'e' in the name is an excellent way to remind me that yes, I am actually about to open a tab to a site that is a distraction at best.

RescueTime

I like the data that RescueTime gives me, and even though I'm not a great fan of the weekly email that shows you how 'productive' you were, the time breakdown is great. Yes, I actually did spend two hours just clearing out my newsfeeds... which seemed like a good idea at the time, but with hindsight it really, really wasn't.

StayFocusd just blocks sites after a time period spent on them. It's harsh, but effective. For me, running my own small business from home, it's extremely effective. I'd like to pretend I'm super disciplined (hey, I created /v/discipline) but I'll be the first to admit that the internet as a whole can very easily distract me from whatever I should be working on. Unfortunately StayFocusd is Chrome only, but there are alternatives for Firefox such as Leechblock. I have not used Leechblock, so I don't feel comfortable recommending it to anyone, so if anyone has any experience please post.

StayFocusd in the Chrome Webstore

Voat itself is an exercise in restraint for me. It's too easy to get carried away, and just browse, but this sub is my responsibility now. If anything I post here helps anyone else struggling with procrastination, focus and discipline in their personal lives that will have been time well spent.

We're still a tiny community, but if anyone has any other great tools that they use please post them.
Two very useful apps / plugins / tools to stay on track while on the computer
